marco_privacy: :loudspeaker: New Consent Ledger + Revocation flow for Private/VPC uploads goes live 2026-12-01. This covers provenance, observability payloads, and assisted debug bundles. Docs: https://go.redwood/consent-ledger
ella_prod: Can we paste a short FAQ for AEs?
marco_privacy: Yes 1) What it is: an immutable consent ledger recording who consented, what was uploaded, TTL, and auditor-visible hashes. 2) Uploads require a signed consent token tied to a contract or approver identity. 3) Customers can revoke consent; revocation prevents new uploads and marks prior uploads with a revocation flag for auditors.
raj_security: Technical quicknotes:
raj_security: • Consent tokens are JWTs signed by customer or Redwood (mutually agreed).
raj_security: • Uploads include a consent-hash in metadata; the ledger stores only consent metadata and artifact hashes (no plaintext payload).
raj_security: • Revocation API invalidates tokens and emits an audit event; revoked uploads remain in storage but get flagged and can be included in auditor export with provenance of revocation.
legal_consent: Legal notes: revocation does not retroactively remove data already received; it prevents further uploads and creates an audit trail. Some regulated customers may require an explicit contract clause to support revocation workflows. Route exceptions to legal_consent@redwood.com.
ops-bot: Policy created: CONSENT-LEDGER-2026 assigned to marco_privacy (due 2026-11-15).
docs: Short CLI examples for customer copy below. We'll publish full FAQ and auditor export format next week.
docs: ```
# create consent token (customer signs or use Redwood sign-on per contract)
redwoodctl consent create --scope "assist-upload" --ttl 7d --approver "ae@example.com" --signer redwood
# upload bundle (requires consent token)
redwoodctl private upload ./bundle.zip --consent-token <JWT> --notify-support true
# revoke consent (customer or approver)
redwoodctl consent revoke --token-id <id> --reason "project closed"
```
support_lead: Support offering: a one-time Assisted Upload Review SKU will be available for customers who want us to ingest artifacts before revocation. Sales ops: add SKU CONSUP-ASSIST to templates.
ella_prod: Sales one-liner: "Consent Ledger provides auditable upload controls and a simple revocation flow so your team controls diagnostic artifact sharing."
marco_privacy: Implementation notes: 1) ledger is append-only; entries are exportable as signed bundles for auditors. 2) we will surface consent state and token expiry in the Console and via API. 3) for air-gapped customers we provide an offline consent signing tool and local ledger export.
raj_security: Security note: consent tokens default to short TTLs (7d) and are rate-limited. We will add alerts for large artifact uploads.
legal_consent: For customers requiring stronger guarantees (e.g., specific retention or deletion commitments) we'll require the Consent Addendum. Legal will post a template and deviation form by EOD.
marco_privacy: Next steps: docs publish (next Tue), support & sales add SKUs (this week), legal finalize addendum (EOD). Outreach to existing Private customers starts next week; those who do not opt in remain on minimal telemetry with no payload uploads.
ella_prod: :thumbsup: Thanks team. If no objections we'll publish the customer notice tomorrow morning.
legal_consent: No objections from legal, route deviations to legal_consent@redwood.com.
